title: Add gating-mode JSON output + metric aggregation + confidence intervals
author: Olivia Grant
release_notes: Eval-harness now supports a guardrails “gating mode” that emits a stable JSON summary including aggregated metrics and 95% confidence intervals, suitable for Optimize apply gating.
description:
## Context
Optimize guardrails gating needs a machine-readable output that: (1) aggregates per-prompt results into suite-level metrics, (2) computes confidence intervals with consistent rules, (3) includes sufficient metadata to be auditable (model version, prompt-set revision, grader versions), and (4) is stable/deterministic so downstream policy evaluation is repeatable.

This PR implements “gating mode” in eval-harness: a JSON output format + aggregation library + CI calculation helpers. This is the core output consumed by the control-plane gating service (see ENG-3915).

## What’s in this PR
- New gating output format (single JSON blob) emitted by CLI and python API
- Aggregation of prompt-level results into metric summaries (mean/percent/pass-rate)
- Confidence interval calculations with metric-type-aware defaults
- Golden-file tests for schema stability + deterministic ordering

## Output format
When running with `--mode=gating` (or `--gating-output <path>`), eval-harness writes `gating_summary.json` with the following top-level structure (illustrative; exact schema in code comments + tests):
- `schema_version`: currently `"gating.v1"`
- `run_id`: UUID
- `started_at` / `finished_at` (UTC ISO8601)
- `suite`: suite name + tags
- `model`: `{ provider, model_id, model_version }`
- `prompt_set`: `{ name, revision, source }`
- `baseline`: `{ model_version, config_fingerprint }` (optional; present when a baseline/candidate comparison is run)
- `candidate`: `{ model_version, config_fingerprint }`
- `metrics`: list of aggregated metric objects
- `artifacts`: pointers to per-prompt outputs (paths/URIs)
- `warnings`: list of strings (e.g. dropped prompts due to invalid grader output)

Each metric in `metrics` includes:
- `name` (canonical metric key)
- `type` (`"mean" | "rate" | "p50" | "p95"` for now; gating primarily uses `mean` and `rate`)
- `n` (# samples included after filtering)
- `value` (candidate aggregate)
- `baseline_value` (if baseline present)
- `delta` and `delta_pct` (if baseline present)
- `ci95_low` / `ci95_high` (for candidate value)
- `baseline_ci95_low` / `baseline_ci95_high` (if baseline present)
- `notes` (string; used for method details / filtering summary)

## Aggregation behavior
- Introduces `MetricAggregator` with a single responsibility: convert a list of prompt-level measurements into an aggregated metric record.
- Filtering rules:
  - Drops prompts with missing metric values.
  - Drops prompts with invalid numeric values (NaN/inf).
  - Records a warning with counts for dropped rows.
- Ordering:
  - Metrics are sorted lexicographically by `name` before serialization to keep output deterministic.

## Confidence intervals
We need intervals that are consistent and reasonably robust across common eval outputs.
- For `rate` metrics (boolean success/failure, e.g. “task_success”): uses Wilson score interval (95%).
- For `mean` metrics:
  - Defaults to bootstrap percentile CI (2.5/97.5) with deterministic seeding derived from `run_id` + metric name.
  - Uses 2000 resamples by default; configurable via `--bootstrap-resamples`.
- For percentiles:
  - Bootstrap percentile CI (same deterministic seeding scheme).

Notes:
- The deterministic seeding is important for gating: the same inputs should yield the same JSON output to avoid “flaky” policy decisions.
- We still include `warnings` in the output if sample sizes are small; we do not hard-fail in eval-harness. The policy layer decides min sample sizes.

## API / CLI changes
- CLI:
  - `--mode gating` enables gating summary emission
  - `--gating-output <path>` sets output directory/file
  - `--bootstrap-resamples <int>` optional
- Python:
  - New `eval_harness.gating.run_gating_eval(...)` helper returning `GatingSummary`
  - `GatingSummary.to_json()` / `write_json(path)`

## Tests
- Added `tests/gating/test_gating_summary_schema.py` golden test for `gating.v1`
- Added unit tests for Wilson interval edge cases (p=0, p=1, small n)
- Added deterministic bootstrap test: repeated runs with same seed produce identical CI bounds

## Files / areas changed (high level)
- `eval_harness/gating/summary.py` (schema + serializer)
- `eval_harness/gating/aggregate.py` (aggregation)
- `eval_harness/stats/confidence_intervals.py` (Wilson + bootstrap)
- `eval_harness/cli.py` (flags + mode routing)
- `tests/gating/*` (golden + unit tests)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add suite-selector helpers for Optimize optimization types (separate PR)
- Add explicit field for grader versions at per-metric level where applicable (currently captured in `artifacts` metadata)

## Screenshots / sample output
Sample snippet (redacted) is included in the golden test fixture; CI verifies stable ordering and stable float formatting.

## Checklist
- [x] Deterministic output (ordering + seeded bootstrap)
- [x] Golden-file schema test
- [x] Unit tests for CI helpers
- [x] Backwards compatible with existing non-gating runs

conversation:
Selene Huang (review): Can we be explicit about schema versioning? We’ll need to pin this in the control plane. Also, can `warnings` be structured instead of strings?

Olivia Grant (author): Added `schema_version: gating.v1` at top-level and a comment in `summary.py` that changes must bump version + update golden fixture. Kept `warnings` as strings for v1 to avoid nested objects; can expand to structured warnings in v2 if we need categories/counts.

Sana Farid (review): Why bootstrap for mean metrics by default vs t-interval? Also concerned about determinism: bootstrap is random.

Olivia Grant (author): Two reasons: (1) many rubric-like metrics aren’t well-approximated by normality at small n, (2) we’re also using it for percentiles. For determinism, we seed RNG using a hash of (`run_id`, metric name) so the same run produces the same CI bounds. Added a test asserting deterministic CI output.

Jonas Weber (review): For `rate` metrics, Wilson is fine. Please add edge-case tests for n=1 and p=0/p=1. Also: do we need baseline CI fields, or can policy compute that downstream?

Olivia Grant (author): Added tests for n=1 + extremes. Baseline CI fields are included because the gating service wants to display them in UI and log them for audit; also avoids policy re-implementing stats.

Sahana Iyer (review): Concerned about golden tests flaking due to float formatting. Also please ensure python version differences won’t reorder dict keys.

Olivia Grant (author): Serialization uses explicit sorted keys for metric list ordering and `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` for nested maps. Float formatting is stabilized by rounding to 6 decimals at serialization time (documented in `summary.py`). Golden fixture updated accordingly.

Selene Huang (review): One more: make sure missing metrics don’t crash the whole run; we should record warnings.

Olivia Grant (author): Done. Missing/invalid values are dropped and aggregated counts land in `warnings`.

Jonas Weber (review): Approved after CI interval tests.

Sana Farid (review): Approved.

Sahana Iyer (review): Approved.

Selene Huang (review): Approved.

Merged by Olivia Grant (squash) into `main`.
